fields.description:
## Context / Problem
`rebar-docker-buildkit-cache-high` (`docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent > 85`, 300/6/6) has been in ALARM since 2026-09-09 22:44 PDT, with daily maxima of 102-115% of the 5 GiB share. Found by the 2026-11-02 read-only ops sweep (session a85e3cd3).

## Root cause (measured read-only on i-00880b2c7f13527c5, 2026-11-03)
- Engine 25.0.16 embeds BuildKit v0.12.6-m.1, and `/etc/docker/daemon.json` (mtime 2026-09-05) still carries only `builder.gc.maxUsedSpace`, a key that BuildKit ignores. `docker buildx inspect` reports an effective keep-bytes of 5.588 GiB, BuildKit's derived default, not 5 GiB.
- The `catty-giddied-hedgehog` fix (change 3022, `ff088a30ea1`) is on the host byte-identical, and its read-only `--print-json` renders `defaultKeepStorage: 5368709120`. But `docker-storage-cap.sh --install` never ran: autodeploy only DETECTS materializer changes (`nginx_materializer_manual`, 2026-09-20 15:22 PDT), and no operator followed up. So the cap is unenforced because a rollout step was never taken, not because of a code defect in the selector.
- Reclaim is not lazy or stalled. Over the last 5 days every 5-minute sample sat at 86-98% of the 5.588 GiB limit BuildKit enforces (peak daily maximum over 35 days: 103.6%), and `docker system df` shows 124 entries, all reclaimable.
- So an ENFORCED cap still sits above 85% of itself: BuildKit fills to its keep-bytes and trims after builds. 85 fires in steady state even when everything works.

## Approach
Two changes, because either alone hides a fault:
1. **Re-threshold** `docker_buildkit_cache_high` to `threshold = 110` (`infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:469`), the documented steady band (86-104% of an enforced limit) plus margin, so it fires only when the cache runs well past its share.
2. **Add an "enforced limit matches the cap" heartbeat**, because a threshold of 110 alone reads OK today (about 96-110% of 5 GiB) while the cap is not enforced. This mirrors `journal_cap_in_effect`:
   - `infra/scripts/docker-storage-cap.sh` gains a side-effect-free `--check-gc-enforced` mode. It prints `1` when the widest `Keep Bytes` from `docker buildx inspect` matches `DOCKER_BUILDKIT_CACHE_BYTES` within `DOCKER_GC_READBACK_TOLERANCE` (`:94`), `0` on mismatch, and nothing (non-zero exit) when unreadable. The comparison is extracted from the existing `report_effective_gc_policy` (`:192`) into one shared helper, so `--install` and the probe cannot disagree.
   - `infra/scripts/observability.sh` §2f publishes `docker_buildkit_gc_enforced` via the existing `heartbeat_value` (`:376`) on EVERY tick, bounded by `clamped "$DOCKER_DF_TIMEOUT"` (`:350`, `:397`), so unreadable reads `-1` (`HEARTBEAT_UNKNOWN`).
   - New alarm `rebar-docker-buildkit-gc-not-enforced` (`docker_buildkit_gc_enforced < 1`, `Minimum`, 300/6/6, `breaching`, SNS on both action lists), the `journal_cap_not_in_effect` shape.

Rewrite the `docker_buildkit_cache_high` description within 1024 bytes. Fix stale `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` lines 946 ("reclaims lazily") and 988 ("Engine >= 25.0 honours maxUsedSpace"), add the new alarm to its "Which alarm fired?" table, and add rows and the threshold note to `infra/runbooks/alarm-window-tuning.md`. Never restart Docker; installing is an operator step. If the mechanism-delta ratchet counts the new metric or mode, add a `mechanism-ok` marker naming this ticket.
Rejected: re-threshold alone (masks the unenforced cap); enforcing the cap alone (the alarm stays red at 85).

## Scope
- `infra/scripts/docker-storage-cap.sh`, `infra/scripts/observability.sh`, `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf`
- `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md`, `infra/runbooks/alarm-window-tuning.md`
- `tests/scripts/test_docker_storage_cap.py`, `tests/scripts/test_observability_docker_storage.py`, `tests/scripts/test_observability_cap_deps.py`, `tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py`, `tests/unit/test_alarm_window_tuning.py`, `tests/unit/test_alarm_description_byte_limit.py` (floors)
Out of scope: the 5 GiB share, the schema boundary (`antitoxic-malophilic-starling`), Docker upgrades, pruning.

## Testing
All offline over the existing PATH stubs (`_bindir` in `test_docker_storage_cap.py`, `_environment` in `test_observability_docker_storage.py`); no Docker, AWS or CI provider. Written failing first:
- `--check-gc-enforced` prints `1` on a matching read-back, `0` on the host shape (5.588GiB vs a 5 GiB cap), and nothing with non-zero exit when inspect prints no policy. It never writes `daemon.json` and never calls `systemctl` or `dockerd`.
- observability publishes `docker_buildkit_gc_enforced` exactly once per run as `1`, `0`, or `-1`, including when `docker system df` fails.
- Terraform: `docker_buildkit_cache_high` is `> 110`; the new alarm is `LessThanThreshold 1`, `Minimum`, `breaching`, SNS on both lists, pinned in the breaching list and in `ALARMED_HEARTBEATS`; alarm-count floors rise by one.

## Deploy
Operator steps, none run by this session: `terraform apply` for the two alarms; on the host `bash /opt/rebar/infra/scripts/docker-storage-cap.sh --install`, then `systemctl restart docker` in a quiet window. `infra/scripts` changes reach the host by autodeploy rsync.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1 — `--check-gc-enforced` prints 1/0/nothing as specified and is side-effect-free; verified by new tests in `tests/scripts/test_docker_storage_cap.py`.
- [ ] AC2 — `--install`'s read-back and `--check-gc-enforced` share one comparison; existing read-back tests stay green.
- [ ] AC3 — observability publishes `docker_buildkit_gc_enforced` every tick (1/0/-1); verified by new tests in `tests/scripts/test_observability_docker_storage.py`.
- [ ] AC4 — Terraform declares threshold 110 and the new alarm with the stated shape; descriptions within 1024 bytes; verified by the Terraform text tests, `terraform fmt -check`, and `validate`.
- [ ] AC5 — runbook lines 946 and 988 are corrected and both runbooks describe the new alarm and threshold.
- [ ] AC6 — targeted tests, `make lint`, and `make typecheck` pass; lands via Gerrit at LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.
- [ ] AC7 [non-codebase] — after the operator install, restart and apply, `docker buildx inspect` reports 5GiB keep-bytes and both alarms are OK; verified read-only.
